text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent midweek newspapers, The Sun and The Gazette, on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Ministry of Health has appointed a committee to investigate allegations of the theft of drugs in hospitals and other health facilities.
- The University of Botswana now offers Masters and Doctorate degree courses in philosophy.

- Ex-president of Zambia, Kenneth Kaunda, reportedly surprised his aides, the Zambian High Commission and the aides of President Sir Ketumile Masire when he paid an unexpected call on the Botswana leader. Later Masire confirmed he had spoken to Kaunda, who, he said, had briefed him on the latest developments in Zambia.
Reports in the same newspaper indicate that Kaunda also called unexpectedly on President Robert Mugabe in Harare, Zimbabwe.

- Police have been given powers to seize vehicles when the drivers cannot produce a valid driving licence, nor enough money to pay a spot fine. Foreign cars, including those driven by tourists, will not be exempt from this law, parliament was told this week.
